title: Preparation, Purification, and Use of Fatty Acid-containing Liposomes
protocol: Transfer lipids to chloroform in a glass vial using gas tight syringes as described.
Evaporate the lipid-chloroform solution under a stream of nitrogen or argon in the fume hood.
Subject the resulting thin film to house vacuum for at least 2 hours to remove any chloroform residue.

Prepare 10 mL of hydration buffer containing 5 mM calcein and 250 mM tris-HCl, pH 8.0 by dissolving 31 mg of calcein powder in 2.5 mL of 1 M tris-HCl buffer and adding another 7.5 mL of deionized water.
Pipette 250 µL of hydration buffer into an empty tube and add 1.875 µL of 10 M NaOH for a final concentration of 75 mM base.
Transfer the solution to the thin film of dry lipid to form vesicles with a total lipid concentration of 0.15 M.
Vortex the resulting mixture for 4-5 seconds using a high-speed vortexer.
Leave the lipid-buffer mixture on a low speed rotating shaker (ca. 30 rpm) to rehydrate, at least overnight.
Apply one filter support to each inner surface of the syringe ports of the extruder using tweezers.
Wet each filter support with 250 mM tris-HCl, pH 8.
Using tweezers, apply one track-etched 100 nm polycarbonate membrane to an extruder O-ring.
Gently push the membrane into the O-ring for good contact between surfaces.
Assemble the extruder carefully without displacing the membrane and filter supports.
Fill an extruder syringe with approximately 0.5 mL of 250 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.
Insert this syringe into one side of the extruder.
Insert an empty syringe into the other side of the extruder.
Push the plunger of the buffer-containing syringe slowly (≤ 50 µL/s) to verify membrane integrity by feeling resistance.
Remove and empty both syringes without cleaning them since they contain identical buffer composition to the liposome preparation.
Load the liposome preparation into one of the two syringes.
Reassemble the extruder with the vesicle sample syringe on the left side and an empty syringe on the right side.
Push the plunger of the vesicle sample syringe very slowly (10-25 µL/s).
Observe the syringe on the right side of the extruder for initial clear buffer entry.
Stop pushing immediately when a small plume of extruded liposomes is observed.
Remove and discard the syringe on the right side containing the initial solution.
Replace the discarded syringe with a new one on the right side of the extruder.
Continue to extrude until the left syringe is empty.
Reverse the orientation of the extruder.
Repeat step 13 for the desired number of cycles (typically 7, 9, or 11).
Gently dispense the contents of the right syringe into an Eppendorf tube.
Place the Eppendorf tube on a low-speed rotating shaker (ca. 30 rpm) for around 0.5 h.
Prepare 5 mL of 250 mM tris-HCl pH 8 hydration buffer by mixing components as specified.
Add 37.5 µL of 10 M NaOH to the hydration buffer.
Pipette 235 µL of pure oleic acid directly into the Falcon tube containing the hydration buffer solution.
Use high-speed (>3000 rpm) vortexer to vortex the mixture for 4-5 s.
Tumble the mixture on a low speed rotating shaker for at least 2 h.
Filter the mobile phase through 0.22 μm syringe filter unit before use.
Purification of vesicles on Sepharose: Remove ca. 5 mL of ethanolic Sepharose 4B slurry from the bottle using a pipette.
Apply this to a disposable 10 mL chromatography column.
Allow the slurry to settle and ethanol flow-through until ethanol approaches top of the resin bed.
Apply 5 mL of deionized water to the top of the resin to wash away ethanol residue.
Apply 250 mM tris-HCl, pH 8 in 1-2 mL portions to the top of the resin, applying a new portion each time liquid level approaches the top of the resin bed.
Repeat buffer application for 3-5 times.
Add another portion of buffer to flush tubing and close stopcock when liquid level in column approaches the top of resin.
Apply extruded vesicles from Section 1 to the top of the resin using a 200 µL pipettor, ensuring even distribution.
Open the stopcock to begin the flow and start collecting fractions into a 96-well plate.
Apply vesicle purification mobile phase to the top of the resin bed in 0.5-1 mL portions as the buffer depletes, taking care not to allow the resin bed to dry out.
Collect in five-drop fractions, collecting at least 36 wells (three rows of a 96-well plate).
Read the 96-well plate on a plate reader (λex=485 nm, λem=515 nm) for fluorescence characterization of purification fractions.
Plot the resulting fluorescence data as fluorescence vs. fraction number.
Repeat the purification and characterization steps to monitor vesicle leakage.
Prepare 1 mL of 50 mM MgCl2 solution in 250 mM tris-HCl pH 8.0 buffer by adding 250 µL of 1 M tris-HCl pH 8.0 buffer and 50 µL of 1 M MgCl2 to 700 µL of DI water.
Vortex the mixture well to ensure thorough mixing.
To give the desired magnesium concentration of 5 mM, mix 0.9 mL of purified vesicles and 100 µL of magnesium solution.
Stir rapidly to minimize vesicle disruption by transient exposure to high local concentrations of magnesium.
Leave the vesicle sample on a tumbler for at least 30 min before repurification.
Prepare and purify vesicles as described in sections 1, 2.1, and 2.2.
Use ½ equivalent KOH instead of NaOH to deprotonate fatty acids.
Prepare 2M potassium citrate solution and adjust pH to 8.0 with KOH.
Premix MgCl2 and potassium citrate at the specified ratio in 250 mM tris-HCl pH 8.0 buffer.
Add premixed magnesium citrate solution to the vesicle sample, briefly vortex.
Always premix magnesium and ligand solution before adding to vesicles.
Leave the vesicle sample on a tumbler for at least 30 min before repurification.
Prepare a dry oleic acid film as described in section 1.1.
Prepare vesicle rehydration buffer with 50 µM fluorescent labeled RNA primer, 150 µM RNA template and 250 mM tris-HCl pH 8.0 containing ½ equivalent KOH relative to oleic acid.
Add 250 µL of rehydration buffer to the lipid film.
Follow step 1.2.2 and 1.2.3 to make vesicles with total 0.15 M lipid concentration.
Prepare small unilamellar monodisperse vesicles by following section 1.3 for vesicle extrusion.
Premix magnesium and citrate stocks.
Mix premixed magnesium and citrate stocks with the vesicle sample to a final lipid concentration of 0.1 M.
Purify vesicles on Sepharose 4B size exclusion column with 250 mM tris-HCl pH 8.0, 0.1 M lipids, and given magnesium and citrate as mobile phase.
Collect vesicle fractions by following section 2.3.
Prepare a 200 mM 2-MeImpG stock solution with 250 mM tris-HCl pH 8.0.
Transfer 150 μL of 2-MeImpG stock solution to 450 μL vesicle sample.
Mix to achieve a final concentration of 75 mM lipid and 50 mM activated monomer.
Start the timer.
Keep the reaction sample tumbling continuously.
(Optional) Transfer 300 µL of reaction solution to one chamber of a lab constructed small-volume liposome dialyzer.
Put 300 μL feeding solution in the other chamber, containing all ingredients at the same concentration as the reaction solution except for RNA-containing vesicles replaced with empty vesicles.
Take a 100 μL aliquot at each time point.
Repurify the aliquot through a Sepharose 4B size exclusion column using 250 mM tris-HCl pH 8.0 as the mobile phase.
Collect vesicle fractions in a 1.5 mL eppendorf tube.
Pipette Triton to the vesicle fractions to achieve a final concentration of approximately 0.1% v/v.
Add 0.5 mL of cold ethanol to the tube and incubate at -20 °C for at least 2 h.
Centrifuge all samples at 16.1×1000 rcf (16.1 × g) for 10 min, then gently pipette out liquids.
Wash RNA pellets with 70% cold ethanol and centrifuge again for 5 min.
Discard liquid from the tube with RNA pellets and place on an 80 °C heat block for 2 min to evaporate residual ethanol.
Dissolve RNA pellets in 50 μL of 8 M Urea with 1xTBE loading buffer.
Mix 200 mL of UreaGel system concentrate, 25 mL of UreaGel system diluent, 25 mL of 10xTBE buffer, 80 µL of TEMED and 250 mg of ammonium persulfate.
Pour the gel mixture between clamped gel plates (35 cm × 45 cm) and insert the comb.
Wait at least 30 minutes for complete polymerization.
Assemble the gel plate onto the gel stand.
Fill the gel boxes with 1xTBE gel running buffer.
Remove the comb and flush the wells with syringe.
Pre-run the gel with 60 W for 30 min.
Heat the samples on an 80 °C heat block for 2 minutes.
Load 5 µL of each sample per well.
Turn on the gel power box and set the gel running at constant watts at 60 W for 2.5 hours.
Disassemble the gel plate from the gel stand, wipe clean the glass, and put the whole plate in a gel scanner to start scanning.
Quantify the gel with ImageQuant TL 1D analysis.
Plot the natural logarithm of the ratio of the amount of primer remaining at a given time point to the initial amount of primer vs. time.
Fit the plot to a line and calculate the pseudo-first order reaction rate.
Prepare a lipid thin film (OA: GMO=9:1) as in section 1.1 with components as in Table 1.2.
Warm GMO to at least 60 °C for complete melting before using.
Prepare vesicle rehydration buffer with 5 µM of each hammerhead ribozyme strand and 250 mM tris-HCl pH 8.0.
Add 250 µL of rehydration buffer to the lipid film.
Follow steps 1.2.2 and 1.2.3 to make vesicles with 0.15 M total lipid concentration.
Purify vesicles on a Sepharose 4B size exclusion column, with 250 mM tris-HCl pH 8.0, 0.15 M mixed lipids as mobile phase.
Prepare magnesium solution and mix with purified vesicles to initiate the self-cleavage reaction.
Take 100 µL of the mixture at each time point and directly repurify this aliquot through a Sepharose 4B size exclusion column with 250 mM tris-HCl pH 8.0 as mobile phase.
Collect the vesicle fraction.
Follow steps 4.3.6 to 4.3.8 to prepare RNA loading sample.
Place commercially casted 15% TBE-Urea gel into gel box and fill the gel box with 1xTBE gel running buffer.
Heat the samples on 80 °C heat block for 1 min.
Load 5 µL of each sample per well.
Run the gel with constant 200 V for around 1 h.
Scan the gel.
Quantify the gel with an analysis software to measure the extent of cleavage.
Prepare an oleic acid thin film with 0.2 mol% of fluorescently labeled lipid.
Rehydrate lipid film with 500 µL 250 mM tris-HCl pH 8.0 to make the vesicle sample 10 mM lipids in total.
Mix 470 µL of oleic acid and 150 mL of 250 mM tris-HCl pH 8.0 containing ½ equivalent NaOH to prepare 150 mL pure fatty acid dialysis buffer with 10 mM total lipids.
Extrude vesicle sample through a 10 µm polycarbonate membrane to remove large aggregates.
Transfer the vesicle sample into a 1 µm large-pore dialysis cassette.
Place the dialysis cassette into a 100-mL beaker containing 30 mL dialysis buffer.
Change the dialysis buffer every 30 min for 5 times to remove free dyes or RNA and small vesicles.
Remove the vesicle sample from the dialysis cassette with a syringe and transfer to an Eppendorf tube.
Pipette 10 µL of vesicles onto a clean standard microscope slide.
Place a glass cover slip over the sample.
Seal the cover glass with transparent nail polish.
Observe the vesicles with a 60X oil-dispersion or similar objective by confocal microscopy using the appropriate laser source for the fluorescently-labeled membrane, RNA or encapsulated dye.
